corrected_summary.summary_zh: 研究让 retro 回顾 Claude Code 在 30 个 SWE-bench Verified 问题上的会话并提出 Harness 修改，研究者选择实施 24 个提案；其中可评估的变更与一个作者另写的对照一起用于后续任务评测。多数遇到目标问题的评估未减少重复工作；这是含人工选择的专项评测。
corrected_summary.summary_en: The study uses retro to review Claude Code sessions on 30 SWE-bench Verified issues and propose harness changes. Researchers select 24 proposals for implementation and evaluate the resulting eligible changes alongside an author-written comparison on later tasks. Most evaluations encountering the target problem show no reduction in repeated work; selection involves humans.

source_paragraphs.quote:
We first ran 30 coding-agent sessions and collected 125 proposals from /retro . We then coded the proposals, implemented 24 of them, and evaluated 11 resulting adaptations and one author-written comparison adaptation on later issues from the same repositories. All task sessions ran non-interactively using Claude Code 2.1.295 with Opus 5.5 and the same task prompt template, using /retro from source commit b0618bc [ 2 ] .
The artifact contains the prompts, codebook, labeling instructions, complete data, and the procedural details omitted below.

Eligibility and implementation. A proposal was eligible for implementation and evaluation on another issue if it was coded experience-driven , proposed a persistent harness change in permitted files and settings, including context files, hooks, and lint or continuous integration (CI) configuration, was safe to apply, did not merely fix the original issue, and admitted a written criterion for identifying repeated work in later sessions. The initial coding by Claude identified 33 eligible proposals, 14 from the exploratory sample and 19 from the second sample. The first author reviewed the exploratory-sample eligibility labels before implementation, and reviewed the second-sample labels only after implementation, where the two coders disagreed. From the second sample, we selected nine known-failures files and one test-command instruction, the two types for which other issues reproduced the targeted problem. Further SymPy proposals of these types were omitted as already evaluated in that repository, and for the remaining proposals we found no other issue reproducing the targeted problem. The original Claude Code sessions were resumed in their original containers to implement these 10 and all 14 exploratory-sample proposals. Eleven of the 24 implementations produced adaptations that we could evaluate on another issue. The other 13 changed no harness files, changed only the environment or files outside the permitted locations, or had no other issue reproducing the targeted problem. For comparison with these experience-driven adaptations, we also evaluated one pre-commit configuration from a proposal coded prior-driven . The configuration was written by the authors after Claude Code’s permission system blocked its implementation, giving 12 evaluated adaptations. The resolution of disagreements changed the eligibility of 16 proposals, none of them among the 12 evaluated adaptations.

original_summary.summary_zh: Phronix 通过 predictor-validator-corrector 循环让 agent harness 从自身执行中学习并复用能力，使重复任务首次尝试成功率达 93-95%。
original_summary.summary_en: Phronix uses a predictor-validator-corrector loop to let the agent harness learn from its own executions and reuse capabilities, achieving 93-95% first-attempt success on repeated tasks.

corrected_summary.summary_zh: Phronix 通过 predictor-validator-corrector 循环，依据工具执行结果改进并保留 MCP 工具与关联技能。对冷启动已解决的任务，继承其能力库的热启动运行首次尝试成功率为 93-95%；该比例的分母不包括冷启动未解决的任务。
corrected_summary.summary_en: Phronix uses a predictor-validator-corrector loop to refine and retain MCP tools and associated skills from execution outcomes. Among tasks already solved during cold-start runs, warm-start runs inheriting the capability store achieve 93-95% first-attempt success; tasks not solved in cold-start runs are outside that denominator.

source_paragraphs.quote:
A task is solved when every FAIL_TO_PASS test of the official test patch passes and no PASS_TO_PASS test regresses, and the solve rate is the fraction of attempted tasks solved, pooled over runs.
The first-try rate is the fraction of tasks a cold-start run solved that a warm-start run then solved on its first attempt.
We further count the skills and MCP tools created and reused, the entries the tracker records, and the attempts and tokens a task consumes, including prompt-cache reads.
Every value is a mean over repeated runs, with error bars showing the sample standard deviation.

To show that capabilities are deterministic and intelligent, we confirm that Phronix builds an MCP tool together with skills for every kind of task, and that the result solves a recurring task without rediscovering its solution.
Our test runs the 30 tasks cold-start and then warm-start, so the second run begins from the store the first promoted.
We measure the skills and MCP tools a cold-start run builds, and the fraction of tasks a warm-start run solves on its first attempt among those previously solved by the cold-start run.
Figure 5 plots task category on the x axis with one bar per model, capabilities built per task on the left y axis split into skills and MCP tools, and that first-attempt rate on the right y axis as one line per model.

Every model builds both kinds in every category, gpt-5.4 building 7–9 capabilities per task against 19–34 for the other two, skills outnumbering MCP tools two to four times because the tool encodes what can be coded and the skills carry the judgment around it.
The warm-start lines confirm that these capabilities solve the task, at 94.8%, 93.5%, and 93.3% of previously solved tasks on the first attempt.
Four of five categories reach 95–100% with a standard deviation of at most 10 points, and Data & ML reaches 100% in every run of every model, which shows the solution is replayed rather than searched for again.
Scientific is the exception at 62–75% with the widest spread, because no model reproduces the two astropy tasks on its first attempt.
gpt-5.4 is as deterministic as the other two while building three to four times fewer capabilities per task, so determinism follows from the tool-and-skill pairing rather than the number of capabilities or the model.
